story: On a sunny Sunday afternoon at 83°F, Gary has walked over to Magnolia Loop, where Donna is cheerfully shuffling flamingos behind a hedge to satisfy the rules. Hal, the stern but fair HOA inspector, reminds her that Section L-02 only allows three ornaments visible from the street and asks to see that count on the lawn. Rosa, patient and optimistic as ever, is heading over too, likely hoping to see how this friendly standoff turns out.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: The lights and speakers are all wired, mounted, and tested inside the garage, and everything checks out. Law L-01 says exterior cart modifications visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, so I shouldn't roll this out until I've filed. Town Hall is the place to do that, and I can't draft or file anything from my house. Keeping the cart in the garage is the right call for now. I'm going to head to Town Hall via Magnolia Loop. It's a sunny Sunday, and I've got work to show for it. Better to do this the right way than have the HOA on my back about it.

parameters.content: Heading out toward Town Hall to get my cart lights and sound system cleared with Architectural Review before I take it on the street.

donna.thought_process: I've told myself three times now to carry the extra flamingos behind the hedge, and Hal just walked up right as I'm about to do it. He's the one I promised. Rather than another round of silent hauling, I should talk to him: show him the street is tidy, keep my word, and maybe mention parade day and Gary. Flamingo count is a law matter (L-02 says three max), so I want Hal to see me doing it right.

parameters.content: Hal, good timing! I'm moving the extra flamingos behind the hedge right now, exactly three stay out front, just like I promised you.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with the binoculars in hand and Donna is right here by her flock. L-02 says three ornaments max visible from the street, and she promised to thin the flock before parade day. The parade has come and gone, so the count is due. I haven't said anything to her about it yet this tick, and a direct question beats guessing from across the street. By the book: ask her plainly, no ambush.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Donna. Parade's over, so about that thinning you promised. Section L-02 says three ornaments visible from the street, and I'd like to see that number on the lawn.

rosa.thought_process: It's past noon and Hal still hasn't shown up for the porch coffee, and I've already been waiting a couple of ticks with the pot brewed. I'm in my kitchen, nobody is in sight, and sitting around watching the walk isn't getting me closer to my goal of building real community. The coffee things are out and the dinner dishes are done, so there's not much left to do here. Better to go outside onto Magnolia Loop, see if Hal or Gary or Donna are around, and gently mention the November 7 Halloween decor deadline in person as a neighborly heads-up rather than sounding like the HOA.

parameters.content: Hal hasn't come up the walk yet, so I'll step out onto the street to find him and say hi to the neighbors.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
